## Requirements (from the contract)

1. Legs added to `scripts/live-capstone.sh`, each independently re-runnable via
   `scripts/live-verify.sh`:
   - (a) ACP — official ACP SDK client (python `agent-client-protocol` or node
     `@zed-industries/agent-client-protocol`, temp dir, never a repo dep) drives
     a live run through `hh acp` over real stdio to a spawned kernel:
     session open → prompt → a permission round → completion; ledger verify +
     offline replay. Fallback: in-tree `AcpClient` over the same real transport
     iff the SDK cannot install or refuses the protocol pin — the record names
     which client ran and why.
   - (b) MCP-lab — official MCP SDK client connects to `hh-mcp-lab` (LabServer)
     and drives Lab ops live: ≥1 experiment op over a live-run-backed arm +
     results/resource reads; the surface-session ledger verifies.
   - (c) SDK/embed — a consumer crate outside the workspace (temp-dir, `path`
     deps on the L4.5 `hharness` facade) drives a live run in process through
     the public `EmbedService` API + asserts verify/replay invariants.
   - (d) Packaged plugins OOP — `hh-memory-store` (memory_store),
     `hh-compact-evict-oldest` (compaction_strategy), `hh-tracker-fixture`
     (work_source_adapter, fleet path) execute out of process through
     `hh-varhost` + `hh-helper` over `plugin_abi/1` during a live run; evidence
     asserts OOP invocation via varhost/helper rows in a run ledger.
2. Dated `docs/build/reports/<date>-live-e2e-surfaces.md` (one row per leg),
   linked from L4.6's capstone report; OPERATIONAL_READINESS surface rows →
   `live-executed` only where a record proves it.
3. USD 0 — local model via HH_LOCAL_BASE_URL/HH_LOCAL_MODEL only; any
   hosted-provider need STOPs and asks.
4. Standing live clauses: secrets by NAME only; `provided: no` → STOP-and-ask;
   `skipped(<reason>)` honest; every leg a `hh-live-evidence/1` record + SPEND
   debit; leak-scan + gitleaks staged gate.
5. Size budget 700 changed lines excl. fixtures/evidence; clear overrun → STOP.
6. Closeout: BUILD_INDEX row 164w, LEDGER advance (done entry + nextTicket
   R4.16), ci-boundary record.

## Orientation notes (Load-list findings)

- `hh acp <definition|ref:>` IS the ACP agent serving verb (crates/hh-cli/src/lab.rs
  `cmd_acp`): `lab.serve{target:acp}` → `AcpArtifact` → `serve_session` over
  stdin/stdout with an `EmbedDriver` on the invocation's own Boundary (spawns
  `hh-kernel serve`). attendance=interactive, approval_mode=manual —
  `security.permission.requested{decider:human}` rows round-trip as blocking
  `session/request_permission` frames (serve.rs `emit_events`).
- ACP pin: `ACP_VERSION="0.1.0"` + `v1-compat`; the official ACP SDK offers its
  own version — expect `ProtocolVersionMismatch` → ticket's fallback clause
  (mirror of capstone-mcp's recorded `2026-07-28` refusal).
- `hh-mcp-lab` = library only: `LabServer` + `serve_stdio`/`serve_http` over an
  `EmbedService`; the s4_11/r2_19 unsafe-pointer thread pattern serves HTTP on
  loopback; in-repo `McpClient<HttpTransport>` is the same-recorded-client
  fallback. Shares `PINNED_MODERN=2026-07-28` — official SDK refusal expected.
- Kernel `instantiate` binds `in_process` only — packaged variants CANNOT bind
  in a run definition (`locality_unsupported`); the varhost spawn path is the
  honest OOP leg (helper execs the variant). `lifecycle.component.bound`/
  `invoked` are kernel_origin rows mintable via `surface_commit_row` on a
  `run_kind = surface` run — the run-ledger landing for varhost rows.
- `hh.submit` is the real completion surface — the model's `hh_submit` call
  dispatches the §5a.2 ceremony; under approval_mode=manual it asks.
- L4.6b (ADR-0381) repaired deterministic replay over effect-dispatching runs —
  byte-identical replay is now expected even with a permission ceremony.
- pricing.json `allocations_usd` has no `L4.6a` key yet — leg budget 0 reads
  alloc 0; add an explicit `"L4.6a": 0` row for honesty.
- Manifests under `plugins/` carry zero-pin `code_pointer` — `seal_package`
  materializes real pins at pack time (varhost test precedent).
